5.text: Google launched Gemini 3.8 for enterprise AI agents, expanded Google Beam to five countries, and began testing Gemini-powered shopping on Flipkart in India. UK regulators proposed giving Android and Chrome users more search-engine choice, YouTube added likeness detection and Gemini editing tools, and Google appealed a $425M privacy verdict.

11.text: Berkshire, under new CEO Greg Abel, built a roughly $37–38 billion Alphabet stake via a $10 billion private placement, making Alphabet its third-largest holding. Other articles cover Berkshire's Lennar and Japanese stock bets, Buffett's exit, and his missed Google investment.

6.text: Alphabet shares fell 3.8% in one session despite no earnings warning, guidance cut, or regulatory news, and Wall Street is concerned about rising capital expenditures and suspended buybacks. Analysts remain bullish, citing Google Cloud growth, Gemini adoption, a $514B backlog, and a low 17x earnings multiple.

7.text: AI infrastructure spending is approaching $200 billion per quarter, with hyperscalers burning about $1 trillion annually and free cash flow falling $440 billion. Analysts and investors warn of debt-funded data centers, off-balance-sheet commitments, and bubble risk; Alphabet appears only as one of the hyperscalers.

8.text: Adobe stock fell about 18% from its August high but rose 24% in three months on AI monetization and a raised 2026 outlook; options imply a $152–$373 range. Alphabet is barely mentioned, so the story bears on it only as sector sentiment.

10.text: Alphabet was among the top contributors to Virtus SGA U.S. Large Cap Growth fund's performance in Q2 2026, alongside Arm Holdings and Nvidia. No further details on Alphabet were given.

4.text: Amazon committed roughly $200 billion in 2026 capex, while Michael Burry warned of massive write-offs within two years from rising leverage and off-balance-sheet AI infrastructure commitments. Alphabet appears only as one of several Big Tech firms grouped in Burry's warning.
